title: Introduce auth-lifecycle-mapper and compact stream facade (py/ts/go)
author: Asha Patel
body:
Motivation: SDKs had small but persistent differences in how credential leases, heartbeats, and resume semantics were expressed. These differences caused incidental reauth calls under load and subtle resume failures when clients transitioned between network conditions. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) an auth-lifecycle-mapper that normalizes lease/ttl semantics and provides a compact policy abstraction across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, and (2) a compact stream facade that exposes lightweight flow-control hints, checkpointed resume tokens, and a smaller ergonomic surface for pull/push streaming usage.

What changed (high level):
- New core: auth-lifecycle-mapper (lib/core/auth_mapper.*) - single policy entrypoint that maps token metadata (issued_at, expires_in, lease_window) into standardized prefetch/refresh decisions and a human-readable policy id. SDK language bindings (py/ts/go) receive the same policy decisions via a tiny protocol shim, reducing language-specific heuristics.
- Compact stream facade: new lightweight facade across SDKs (sdk/python/redwood/stream_facade.py, sdk/typescript/src/stream/facade.ts, sdk/go/stream/facade.go). It: emits flow hints (suggested_batch_ms, soft_deadline_ms), supports checkpointed resume tokens with opaque cursors, and provides a single Read/Write/Checkpoint API set that maps to each SDK's async model.
- Telemetry: added auth.lifecyle.{prefetch,refresh,fail} events and stream.facade.{checkpoint,flow_hint} metrics with consistent tag shapes across languages to aid cross-platform tracing.
- Ergonomics: renamed a few surface methods for symmetry (Python: StreamClient.resume -> StreamClient.checkpoint_resume; TypeScript: stream.resume -> stream.restoreCheckpoint; Go: StreamClient.ResumeCheckpoint). Backwards-compatible shims are provided with deprecation warnings.
- Tests & docs: end-to-end interop tests added to perf-canary harness and new README examples for migration.

Why this is different: instead of each SDK implementing ad-hoc lease/refresh heuristics we centralize decision logic into the auth-lifecycle-mapper which returns compact actions (noop/prefetch/refresh/evict) plus timing hints. This reduces redundant refresh calls and ensures identical behavior in multi-language clients. The compact facade intentionally avoids exposing heavy transport internals while giving enough control for production apps to implement checkpointed resumption and flow-control tuning.

Migration notes: the old resume APIs continue to work but will log a single deprecation warning for one release. Recommended migration steps are included below in the README changes. For teams using custom credential providers, implement the small shim api (get_token_metadata(token) -> {issued_at, expires_in}) to participate in mapped policies.

Testing & rollout: all unit tests run under CI; cross-SDK interop e2e added to perf-canary. Deployment is gradual: feature gated behind a runtime flag in Dedicated so we can A/B traffic for 48h before enabling by default.

Checklist:
- [x] Add auth mapper core and language shims
- [x] Implement compact stream facade in py/ts/go
- [x] Add telemetry and update schema registry
- [x] Add unit + interop e2e tests
- [x] Add migration docs and release notes

Files of particular interest: see files_changed for specific changesets. If you want a short demo of the new facade in Python, see examples/stream_facade_quickstart.py in this PR.

reviews: Miguel Torres (reviewer): Left a few questions around the prefetch jitter algorithm — suggested using a 10-20% backoff for bursty connections. Asha: addressed and added unit tests that simulate jitter (see test_auth_mapper.py).
Sofie Lange (reviewer): Flagged that TS public method rename needs explicit note in CHANGELOG. Asha: added changelog entry and a small codemod script for monorepo customers.
Diego Ramos (approver): Verified interop e2e locally and approved. Small comment to add a timeout guard on the Go resume path; addressed in b1c0d44.
ci_summary: CI: lint(py/ts/go) ✓, unit tests ✓, e2e perf-canary ✓. One transient integration job failed on first run (network flake), rerun passed.
release_notes: Added auth-lifecycle-mapper (normalizes token lease and prefetch logic across SDKs); introduced compact stream facade with checkpointed resume tokens and flow-control hints; minor API renames with backward-compatible shims; updated telemetry tags for auth/stream events. See docs/sdk-migration for migration steps.
